reject_when: queued request waits longer than 500 ms
accept_when: queue has capacity and a slot opens before 500 ms
policy.implementation: asyncio SLAAdmissionController in front of vLLM OpenAI completions; vLLM internals unmodified
policy.note: Policy is fixed before benchmarking and not changed mid-run.

24.tradeoff: Admission lowers/controls completed latency by rejecting or timing out 33.33% of offered load; not a free latency win.

32.tradeoff: Admission lowers/controls completed latency by rejecting or timing out 50.0% of offered load; not a free latency win.

recommendation: Recommend enabling SLA-aware admission as a protective overload control (max_active=16, queue=16, timeout=500ms) in front of W8A8+prefix-cache serving. Under this I.3 overload (prefix cache ON), completed p95 already stayed <1s without admission; admission did not buy a free latency win—at offered=24 it slightly improved p95 (−3.5%) while rejecting 33.3%, and at offered=32 completed p95 rose slightly (queue wait in E2E) while rejecting 50%. Primary benefit: bounded queue, explicit timeout/reject instead of unbounded accept-all, and capped active concurrency at the I.1 saturation point.

interpretation.prefix_cache_effect: I.2 prefix caching keeps overload p95 well under the 1s budget even without admission (~704–707 ms at offered 24/32 vs I.1 no-cache c16 p95 923.5 ms).
interpretation.admission_role: protective load-shedding / bounded-queue control, not latency magic
interpretation.fairness: Always read p95 together with rejection_rate and throughput_preserved
